title: Breaking a pin
line: Block, move the piece behind, or attack the pinning piece.

steps.text: Your knight is pinned: it may not move, because the bishop would then give check. Until the pin is broken, it is stuck.
The first way: attack the pinning piece. Push a pawn at the bishop.

also.c8d7: That breaks the pin too, by blocking. This step attacks the bishop.

steps.hint: One of your pawns can attack the bishop in one step.
steps.after: The bishop stepped back, but it still pins the knight.

steps.text: Attack it again with the next pawn. If it keeps running, it must leave the line.
steps.after: The bishop has left the line to your king: the pin is gone.

steps.text: The second way: block. Here the bishop pins your knight to the queen behind it.
Put your other bishop between the knight and the queen.
steps.after: Now the knight can move: only the bishop behind it would be attacked, and the bishop is guarded.

steps.text: The third way: move the piece behind. Here your knight is pinned to your king again.
Castle. Your king leaves the bishop's line, and the knight is free to move.
steps.after: No king behind the knight, no pin.

summary: Three ways out of a pin: chase the pinning piece, put another piece in its line, or move the piece behind.
